title: "Day 10: Prompting only"

The following code was used to call Gemini:

```{r}
library(ellmer)

prompt <- "Write R code to create a map for the 30 Day Map Challenge, preferably using `ggplot2`. The prompt is 'prompting only' so you have free reign to decide on the data, map type, and styling. The output should be saved as a PNG file, and include source data attribution in the caption. The map title should summarise the main message, and the subtitle should provide additional details about the data."

chat <- chat_google_gemini(model = "gemini-3.5-flash-lite")
chat$chat(prompt)
```

The output is provided (essentially verbatim) below. Notes:

* I didn't ask for a Markdown/Quarto document, I only asked for R code which I would generally write in a script.
* I have replaced the code block sections below from ` ```{r} ` to ` ```{r} ` so that they actually run.
* I also edited the file name used to save the chart. I want it in a specific format but didn't make that clear from the prompt. It originally saved as `manhattan_grid_map.png`.
* I also split the code into multiple code blocks to avoid re-running the OpenStreetMap queries every time.

# Output

For the **#30DayMapChallenge** (specifically for a "Prompting Only" theme, where the
map is generated entirely through code/algorithmic prompting), this R script creates
a stunning, minimalist map of **Manhattan’s street grid**, downloaded directly via 
the `osmdata` (OpenStreetMap) package.

It uses `ggplot2` to style the different road hierarchies (highways, major streets, 
and minor streets) with a sleek, dark-mode aesthetic.

### Prerequisites

You will need to install the following packages if you haven't already:

```{r}
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "osmdata", "sf", "showtext"))
```

### R Code

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(osmdata)
library(sf)
library(showtext)

# Enable Google Fonts for better typography
font_add_google("Cinzel", "cinzel")
font_add_google("Lato", "lato")
showtext_auto()

# 1. RETRIEVE DATA FROM OPENSTREETMAP ------------------------------------------

# Define the bounding box for Manhattan, New York City
manhattan_bbox <- getbb("Manhattan, New York City, USA")

# Query OpenStreetMap for different road types
# A. Highways / Major Arterials
q_highways <- manhattan_bbox %>%
  opq() %>%
  add_osm_feature(key = "highway", 
                  value = c("motorway", "trunk", "primary", "secondary"))

# B. Minor Streets / Local Roads
q_streets <- manhattan_bbox %>%
  opq() %>%
  add_osm_feature(key = "highway", 
                  value = c("tertiary", "residential", "living_street", 
"unclassified"))

# Convert queries to sf objects
sf_highways <- osmdata_sf(q_highways)
sf_streets <- osmdata_sf(q_streets)

# Extract the linestrings
roads_highways <- sf_highways$osm_lines
roads_streets <- sf_streets$osm_lines


# 2. PLOT WITH GGPLOT2 ---------------------------------------------------------

# Define color palette (Dark mode aesthetic)
bg_color <- "#0d1117"       # Very dark blue/black
highway_color <- "#ff5e62"  # Vibrant coral/red for major roads
street_color <- "#c9d1d9"   # Soft light grey for local grid
```

```{r}
p <- ggplot() +
  # Plot minor streets first (background layer)
  geom_sf(data = roads_streets, 
          color = street_color, 
          linewidth = 0.15, 
          alpha = 0.5) +
  
  # Plot highways on top (foreground layer)
  geom_sf(data = roads_highways, 
          color = highway_color, 
          linewidth = 0.4, 
          alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # Set coordinate system to maintain proper aspect ratio for NYC
  coord_sf(xlim = c(manhattan_bbox[1, 1], manhattan_bbox[1, 2]),
           ylim = c(manhattan_bbox[2, 1], manhattan_bbox[2, 2]),
           expand = FALSE) +
  
  # Theme and styling
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = bg_color, color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = bg_color, color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 40, r = 40, b = 40, l = 40),
    
    # Title formatting
    plot.title = element_text(
      family = "cinzel",
      size = 28,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#ffffff",
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(b = 10)
    ),
    
    # Subtitle formatting
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      family = "lato",
      size = 12,
      color = "#8b949e",
      hjust = 0,
      lineheight = 1.3,
      margin = margin(b = 20)
    ),
    
    # Caption formatting
    plot.caption = element_text(
      family = "lato",
      size = 9,
      color = "#484f58",
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(t = 20)
    )
  ) +
  
  # Labels
  labs(
    title = "THE MANHATTAN GRID",
    subtitle = "An algorithmic extraction of New York City's iconic urban fabric, 
\nhighlighting the contrast between major arterial corridors and the local street 
matrix.",
    caption = "Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors | Created with R & ggplot2 for 
#30DayMapChallenge"
  )


# 3. SAVE THE OUTPUT -----------------------------------------------------------

# Save as a high-resolution PNG file suitable for social media sharing
ggsave(
  filename = "2026/maps/day_10_v0.png",
  plot = p,
  width = 8,
  height = 10,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = bg_color
)

print("Map successfully created and saved as '2026/maps/day_10_v0.png'!")
```

### Features of this Map:
1. **Data Source:** Pulls live, highly accurate vector data directly from 
**OpenStreetMap** using `osmdata`.
2. **Visual Hierarchy:** Differentiates between major highways/arterials (glowing 
coral) and minor residential streets (muted grey) to emphasize traffic flow 
patterns.
3. **Typography:** Uses Google Fonts (`Cinzel` for an architectural header and 
`Lato` for clean body text) via the `showtext` package.
4. **Theme:** Designed with a striking dark-mode palette that makes the street grid 
pop.
5. **Attribution:** Properly credits OpenStreetMap in the caption, as required by 
their terms of use.

# Nicola's edits

Keep the data, but improve the way the chart looks:

```{r}
library(ggtext)
library(ggview)
showtext_opts(dpi = 300)

```

```{r}
ggplot() +
  # Plot minor streets first (background layer)
  geom_sf(data = roads_streets, 
          color = street_color, 
          linewidth = 0.15, 
          alpha = 0.5) +
  
  # Plot highways on top (foreground layer)
  geom_sf(data = roads_highways, 
          color = highway_color, 
          linewidth = 0.4, 
          alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # Set coordinate system to maintain proper aspect ratio for NYC
  coord_sf(xlim = c(manhattan_bbox[1, 1], manhattan_bbox[1, 2]),
           ylim = c(manhattan_bbox[2, 1], manhattan_bbox[2, 2]),
           expand = FALSE) +
  
  # Theme and styling
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = bg_color, color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = bg_color, color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 0, 10, 0),
    
    # Title formatting
    plot.title = element_textbox_simple(
      family = "cinzel",
      size = rel(1.4),
      face = "bold",
      color = "#ffffff",
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(b = 10)
    ),
    
    # Subtitle formatting
    plot.subtitle = element_textbox_simple(
      family = "lato",
      size = rel(1),
      color = "#8b949e",
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(b = 10)
    ),
    
    # Caption formatting
    plot.caption = element_textbox_simple(
      family = "lato",
      size = rel(0.9),
      color = "#484f58",
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(t = 10)
    )
  ) +
  
  # Labels
  labs(
    title = "THE MANHATTAN GRID",
    subtitle = "An algorithmic extraction of New York City's iconic urban fabric,  highlighting the contrast between major arterial corridors and the local street matrix.",
    caption = "Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors | Created with R & ggplot2 for 
#30DayMapChallenge"
  ) +
  canvas(
    width = 5, height = 10,
    units = "in", bg = bg_color,
    dpi = 300
  ) -> p


# 3. SAVE THE OUTPUT -----------------------------------------------------------

save_ggplot(
  plot = p,
  file = "2026/maps/day_10.png"
)

print("Map successfully created and saved as '2026/maps/day_10.png'!")
```
